articles.headline: Lamar County Schools introducing weapons detectors, AI camera detection
articles.image_alt: Weapons detection scanners at school entrance
articles.excerpt: Lamar County Schools will make weapons detection a daily practice at every middle and high school campus this year, pairing walk-through detectors with AI camera monitoring as districts across Mississippi harden campuses before classes resume.

articles.headline: Colt Gray, Georgia school shooter, pleads guilty and victims deliver emotional statements in court
articles.image_alt: Courtroom scene at Apalachee plea hearing
articles.excerpt: Colt Gray pleaded guilty to all 55 counts in the 2024 Apalachee High School shooting that killed teachers Richard Aspinwall and Cristina Irimie and two students. Families and wounded survivors urged the judge to deny any possibility of parole.

articles.headline: Dorchester County agencies hold active shooter drill ahead of new school year
articles.image_alt: First responders during school safety drill
articles.excerpt: With the new school year weeks away, first responders and school officials in Dorchester County ran worst-case active shooter scenarios at Williams Memorial Elementary, drilling the coordination needed to protect educators and students in a real attack.

articles.headline: Teacher Sues Howard Co. Board Of Education: Report
articles.excerpt: A math specialist at Bonnie Branch Middle School is suing the Howard County Board of Education for $750,000, alleging it failed to protect her after a parent blocked her in a conference room in 2023 — an encounter she says later triggered a stroke.

articles.headline: First Responders to Meet for Annual School Safety Planning
articles.excerpt: Law enforcement, fire, EMS, emergency dispatchers, school resource officers and school administrators will gather ahead of the new school year to review and strengthen safety procedures across local campuses.

articles.headline: AFT Re-elects Officers, Hears from Union and Political Leaders, Passes Suite of Resolutions at 2026 Convention
articles.excerpt: At its 2026 convention, the AFT adopted a resolution declaring violence is never 'part of the job,' demanding enforceable workplace violence protections for teachers and school staff — noting 1 in 4 nonfatal workplace violence incidents target school employees.

articles.headline: Opelousas woman accused of terrorizing, assault on teacher
articles.image_alt: St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office insignia
articles.excerpt: A 25-year-old Opelousas woman was arrested after allegedly threatening a school paraprofessional and the St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office. She faces a felony terrorizing count and four felony counts of assault on a school teacher.

articles.headline: Ascension Public Schools rolling out upgrades ahead of new school year
articles.excerpt: The Louisiana district is investing $2.5 million in AI-powered weapons detection systems at every campus and requiring clear backpacks and water bottles for all students as part of a broader push for faster, safer school entry.

articles.headline: Public schools across Kentucky will see changes starting Wednesday
articles.image_alt: School bus outside a Kentucky school
articles.excerpt: Kentucky's Senate Bill 101 takes effect July 15, requiring districts to expel students in grades 6-12 for at least a year if they injure or attempt to injure school staff. The law answers teacher unions' calls to put educator safety first, mandating law enforcement reporting of assaults.

articles.headline: Detroit man charged in fatal shooting of custodian outside Chrysler Elementary School
articles.image_alt: Police photo related to school shooting case
articles.excerpt: Prosecutors charged Kevin Flagg, 43, with second-degree murder in the July 2 shooting of Devin Burns, a 25-year-old contracted custodian for Detroit Public Schools, killed in the Chrysler Elementary parking lot after a dispute escalated. Flagg returns to court July 20.

archive.headline: School shootings in the US: Fast facts
archive.excerpt: CNN's updated tracker counts at least 31 school shootings in the U.S. so far in 2026 — 21 on K-12 grounds — leaving at least 22 people dead and 23 injured, underscoring the threat educators and staff face on campus.

archive.headline: Henry County schools invest in teachers, safety ahead of new school year
archive.excerpt: Henry County's school board approved budget updates directing new money to higher employee pay and additional school security ahead of the 2026-27 year — a district-level bet that safer campuses help retain educators.

archive.headline: Gov. Green signs key measures to strengthen Hawaiʻi's education system
archive.excerpt: Hawaiʻi's HB 1888 makes harassment of school employees a misdemeanor, requires threats be reported to police within 48 hours, and lets the attorney general help educators obtain restraining orders against aggressors.

archive.headline: Student busted with gun at Manhattan high school: NYPD
archive.excerpt: A 17-year-old was arrested after an unannounced scanning at West Side High School turned up a loaded, defaced 9mm pistol in his bag. He faces three counts of criminal possession of a weapon; no one was injured.

archive.headline: Fitzgerald Public Schools cancels summer classes, camp after threatening email
archive.excerpt: Fitzgerald Public Schools in Warren, Michigan canceled all summer classes and camp programming after district leaders received a threatening email targeting multiple school buildings. Officials suspended programs while working with law enforcement to assess the threat.

archive.headline: Now It's Student Attacks on Teachers: Are Our Schools Out of Control?
archive.excerpt: A national commentary surveys the string of recent student attacks on teachers, from a Maryland stabbing to a Montana classroom beating, and asks whether schools have lost the authority to protect the adults in the classroom as discipline structures erode.

archive.headline: Lockdown lifted at Edinburg North High School after 'no credible threat' found following reports of a weapon on campus
archive.excerpt: Edinburg North High School in Texas locked down July 6 after a parent reported a possible weapon on campus. Officers searched the school and lifted the lockdown within 40 minutes after finding no credible threat, though staff and parents said the scare renewed safety concerns.

archive.headline: California schools must follow new cellphone, bathroom and safety laws
archive.excerpt: New California laws taking effect this school year require districts to restrict student cellphone use and expand campus safety measures, including staff training requirements and broader background checks for school employees.

archive.headline: 'Ricky and Alyssa's Law' will require all GA public schools to install mobile panic alert systems beginning July 1
archive.excerpt: Beginning July 1, Georgia's 'Ricky and Alyssa's Law' requires every public school to deploy mobile panic-alert devices, putting an emergency button in the hands of every teacher and administrator and linking directly to first responders. It honors two victims of school violence.

archive.headline: Minnesota's anonymous school threat reporting system law begins July 1
archive.excerpt: A Minnesota law taking effect July 1 requires every public school district and charter school to provide an anonymous way to report threats via app, website, or hotline, giving students and staff a faster channel to flag danger to administrators before it escalates.

archive.headline: July 1: New Mississippi laws take effect today
archive.excerpt: Among the new Mississippi laws taking effect July 1: anyone 18 or younger who commits a crime with a firearm will now be automatically charged as an adult. Backers frame the tougher stance as a deterrent to the weapons increasingly turning up on and around school campuses.

archive.headline: Teachers say they're being bitten, headbutted and bruised while trying to manage classrooms
archive.excerpt: A Long Beach Post analysis of hundreds of workers' comp claims found 72 LBUSD employees severely hurt by a student in 2024-25, up from 49 three years earlier — with educators reporting bites, headbutts and lasting injuries.
